_about: Phase 1 of the Universal PCB AI Engine (PCB_AI_ARCHITECTURE.md stages 1-3+5). Drives tools/pcb_reasoning.py. Classifies each component from PIN BEHAVIOR (pin names + net names + connection graph), NOT from component-name templates, then scores criticality, picks the placement anchor, and emits per-role constraints. Every signature/weight/threshold is here -- no Python literals, no component-name lists. Signatures are substring/pattern matches on UPPERCASED pin/net names, so an unseen part classifies by behaviour. enabled=false makes the tool a no-op.
_role_confidence_doc: How SURE the engine is about each role, so a placer/router (or the user) can treat a low-confidence role as a guess rather than fact. Base value by decision path: a device CLASS read from lib_id is near-certain (lib_class_hint); a pin-behaviour rule match is strong but weaker (pin_behaviour_rule); a fallback to 'passive' with no signature is a guess (fallback_passive). A non-anchor controller demoted to peripheral_ic drops to controller_demoted. corroboration_per_char adds a small bonus per agreeing electrical character (capped at corroboration_max_bonus, overall clamped to max_confidence) so a role backed by several signals reads as more certain. Components with confidence < low_confidence_threshold are listed under report.low_confidence. enabled=false omits all confidence fields -> the sidecar stays byte-identical to the pre-feature output.
_dynamic_doc: The engine classifies from PIN BEHAVIOUR + NET TOPOLOGY first (anchor, emergent domain, and most roles need no catalog at all — verified by ablation). Two OPTIONAL refinements handle distinctions that pin behaviour physically cannot make: device CLASS from lib_id (TVS vs LED) and current tier from footprint PACKAGE (power vs small-signal FET). These read a part's electrical CLASS / physical PACKAGE, never its part number, and they generalise to any unseen part. Set either flag false for pure pin+topology reasoning (the engine degrades gracefully — see ablation). At PCB stage the package tier can instead be derived from real pad-copper AREA (fully geometric).
_match_doc: Token-aware matcher tuning (the engine's only algorithm constants — no component knowledge). A pattern hits a name if it is a whole token, a token prefix of >= token_prefix_min chars, or a substring of >= substring_min chars. Stops short tokens like 'IN' matching inside 'TIMING'.
_layer_recommendation_doc: R0b: 2 vs 4 layer recommendation, derived from board SIGNALS only — part count, high-speed characters, emergent domains — never a component list. 4-layer when parts >= parts_for_4layer, OR any high-speed char is present (needs a solid reference plane), OR an emergent domain in domains_force_4layer appears. Reported as recommended_layers; advisory (does not force the stackup).
_controller_sig_doc: A pin-behaviour 'controller' on a non-anchor part is demoted to peripheral_ic unless it shows one of these real-controller characters (its own clock or a high-speed bus). Distinguishes an MCU from an I2C sensor.
_pin_signatures_doc: Matched as substrings against each component's UPPERCASED pin names (from IR net pins 'REF.PINNAME') and the names of the nets it touches. A component accumulates a set of 'characters' from its hits.
_net_signatures_doc: Matched against UPPERCASED net names. Emergent domain hints aggregated across the whole board (outputs, not inputs).
_pin_only_chars_doc: Characters that may ONLY be set from a component's own PIN names, never from the nets it touches. Being wired to a buck 'SW' node does not make an inductor/diode/resistor a switch -- only a part with its OWN GATE/DRAIN/SOURCE (or an IC's SW) pin is a switch.
_lib_class_hints_doc: Device CLASS read from the KiCad lib_id category (e.g. 'Regulator_Switching', 'Transistor_FET', 'RF_GPS', 'D_TVS', 'Device:L'). This is the part's electrical class -- as legitimate a signal as its refdes prefix (C=cap) or its footprint package -- NOT a part-number template. A lib-class hit wins over the pin-behaviour role_rules. 'mosfet' is tiered to power vs small-signal by footprint (power_packages).
_power_packages_doc: Footprint substrings that indicate a power package (carries amps, needs copper + thermal). A FET in one of these is a power_switch; otherwise it is a small_signal_switch (no width/thermal). Same idea distinguishes a buck pack-current FET from a milliamp cell-balancing FET.
_role_rules_doc: Ordered. First matching rule sets the component role. 'pins_min'/'pins_max' bound the component pin count; 'has' requires ALL listed characters; 'any' requires ANY; 'prefix' restricts to a refdes prefix (a legitimate device-class hint, e.g. C=capacitor, not a part-name template). 'two_pin_across' = a 2-pin part bridging the two listed character classes (e.g. power+ground -> decoupling).
_score_doc: anchor score = sum of weighted terms. connection_count = # distinct nets touched; pin_count from footprint; criticality from criticality_class[role]; power_level = 1 if it touches a power rail. Highest score => placement anchor.
_constraint_merge_doc: Characters whose constraints are merged onto a part IN ADDITION to its role constraints (isolation/routing needs that hold regardless of role, e.g. a series resistor on a USB pair still needs length_match). power/power_switch are deliberately EXCLUDED so a small-signal FET that merely carries a power_switch character does NOT inherit high-current width/thermal — that is decided by its role (footprint-tiered).
_constraints_doc: Per-role placement/routing constraints emitted into the sidecar for Phase 2/3 to consume. keep_close_to_anchor: stay within max_dist_mm of the anchor pin it shares a net with. keep_away_from: min_gap_mm from components of the listed characters (noise isolation). width_by_current: route widened per ampacity (R2). keepout: reserve copper-free area. All distances in mm.
_emergent_domains_doc: Reported (not used as input). A board is tagged with every domain whose trigger characters appear, so a tracker can be RF+power+digital at once.
